title: Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

reading.body:
This is a detection failure in an autonomous driving system, at the point where the vehicle decides what is in its path and whether to slow. The car was in autonomous mode and a human safety operator was on board, and it still ran over the duck without slowing or stopping. A person able to intervene was present and the collision happened anyway, which puts the failure in the perception and response path rather than in the absence of supervision.

Catching it would have required the system to treat a small animal in the roadway as an obstacle, or testing that exercised that scenario before the vehicle met it on a public street. Avride's remedy was to review vehicle data, replay the scene in simulation, exclude certain streets around the lake and run controlled experiments, which is the shape of a gap found after the fact rather than a rule applied incorrectly.

What is not established is fault. A resident's claim that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign is an allegation that Avride disputed using its own vehicle data, and that data has not been independently confirmed. The reporting contains no finding of intent and no regulatory conclusion.

reports.title: A self-driving car in Texas hit and killed a mother duck, sparking neighborhood outrage
Residents say self-driving car killed duck in Mueller
Self-driving car runs over Mueller Lake Park duck, raising safety concerns
Mueller residents upset after self-driving car runs over, kills duck

summary:
A self-driving car operated by Avride struck and killed a mother duck in the Mueller Lake neighborhood of Austin, Texas, prompting significant community concern about autonomous vehicles. The incident occurred when the vehicle, which was in autonomous mode with a human safety operator present, ran over the duck without slowing down or stopping. The duck had been nesting in a pot outside a local Italian restaurant, making it familiar to residents, which intensified their outrage. Local residents have since placed the duck's eggs in an incubator for safekeeping.

In response to the incident, Avride confirmed the vehicle was operating autonomously at the time and investigated the event by reviewing vehicle data and replaying the scene in simulation. The company also addressed a resident's claim that the vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign, stating that data showed the vehicle made complete and appropriate stops at all relevant signs. Avride has adjusted its testing operations by excluding certain streets around the lake and is now running controlled experiments to improve the technology and prevent similar situations, while continuing autonomous vehicle testing in other Austin areas.
